newsitem.title: USA: DT Industries buys Lucas Assembly assets.
newsitem.headline: DT Industries buys Lucas Assembly assets.

text.p: DT Industries Inc said Tuesday it had completed the acquisition of the assets of Lucas Assembly and Test Systems, a division of LucasVarity Plc, for $49 million.
Lucas Assembly designs and makes integrated assembly and testing systems for automotive original equipment manufacturers and their tier-one suppliers.
The purchase is subject to final balance sheet adjustments and was funded through DT's recently renegotiated $175 million multi-currency credit facility, DT said.
The Lucas Assembly business has manufacturing facilities in Michigan and in Buckingham, England, and Koblenz, Germany.
As part of LucasVarity, the division recorded sales of about $112 million during the year ended January 31, 1997, with operating profit of about $4.4 million before nonrecurring items.
For the five months ended June 30, Lucas Assembly's sales totaled about $47 million, with operating profit of about $2.3 million.

"This is a very strategic fit that will complement operations in our DT Automation Group," DT President Stephen Gore said in a statement. "It brings a strong European presence in sales, service and manufacturing and provides significant cross-selling opportunities, both for the Assembly Technology & Test business and for our existing businesses."

Lucas Assembly designs and manufactures integrated assembly and testing systems for fuel, engine, transmission and chassis applications. About two-thirds of its sales are to North America, and one-third to Europe.
